votes.reason: Healthcare is my top sector and JNJ is one of the leaders I named near its highs (+2.7% on the week, +14.8% over 12 weeks), so it gives the book the low-beta defensive I want going into Friday's CPI while staying out of LLY, the weak heavyweight that is my main sector risk, and the Sep 8-9 drug-pricing items are a risk I already named rather than a reason to pass.

JPM is the largest money-center bank in Financials, which I rated as working on either side of the CPI print, and it belongs to the rate-driven bank group I said is leading rather than the payments and asset-manager names I flagged as the risk, even though it lagged WFC and C last week at +0.3%.

Energy is the sector I said gains from the Hormuz and US-Iran shocks, and VLO has been leading it (+5.2% on the week, +24% over four weeks); as a refiner that earns on product margins it is less tied than crude producers to my main risk of a ceasefire unwinding the war premium, and the 15% cap handles its volatility.

PGR sits in Financials, the one sector I rated as working on either side of Friday's CPI, and its short-duration bond portfolio reinvests at the higher short rates my thesis expects, while its drivers stay apart from the payments and asset-manager weakness I named as the sector's risk.

Technology is my cool-CPI leg and NVDA's +5.9% week is the evidence behind it, since semis were bought rather than sold into the hawkish jobs print, and ORCL's Sep 10 report is the in-window AI-spending catalyst I named, so a 10% seat fits even though core CPI at 0.3% or more with the 10Y above 4.85% would break it.
